sorries.obstruction: Zassenhaus/Auslander step: there is eps > 0 such that elements of rho(Gamma) (rotation parts on the screen, a section of P0bar) within eps of 1 commute. True by Auslander's theorem (Raghunathan Thm 8.24, number unchecked, applied to Gamma ∩ G^0 -- finite index, G^0 = K^0 x| N connected, same identity component H^0 of the rotation-part closure: (closure(Gamma N))^0 solvable for N = null rotations x translations, closed connected nilpotent normal in G = K x| N) + Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem (closure of rho(Gamma) a compact Lie group, identity component open) + compact connected solvable => torus; or via amenability + Tits' alternative. mathlib has no Lie groups, no Cartan theorem, no structure theory of compact groups, no Tits alternative at fabf563a.

findings: The whole proof of TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull reduces, with everything else proved, to one LOCAL statement about the closure of the rotation parts (a neighbourhood of 1 in which they commute); discreteness is spent only there, ellipticity only in the commutator step (an elliptic Lorentz map fixing v0 with trivial action on P0bar is the identity). The free quaternion pair of Nonloxodromic finding (7) violates exactly that local statement (rho(Gamma) dense in a copy of SU(2)) and no other step.

Barbot's 'natural action of L(Gamma)' on P0bar (l.2627-2629) is realised as the unital endomorphism rho(A) = pi A pi + (1 - pi) of M^n, pi the projection on the screen {v0, e0}^perp along span{v0, e0}; it is multiplicative on the stabiliser of v0 and uniformly bounded (it preserves qbar0).
questions: The citation Raghunathan, Discrete subgroups of Lie groups, Thm 8.24 (Auslander) is from memory; references/ has no copy. If the master session wants the sorry discharged as a named external (DEC-36 style) instead, the honest unit is exactly exists_commute_screenRot_of_discrete's statement.

The existing named external AuslanderCarriereDalbo d (Flat/Externals, bthm:ausl) does not discharge the sorry by itself: it gives (closure L(Gamma))^0 nilpotent, but the local statement also needs that identity component to be OPEN in the closure (Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem), which mathlib lacks; recorded in the SCOPE.

kb_proposals: A quotient like Barbot's P0bar = v0^perp / R v0 is cheapest as a SECTION: the screen {v0, e0}^perp with Submodule.projection, and the induced action as the unital endomorphism pi A pi + (1 - pi) of M^n -- multiplicative on the stabiliser, normed for free (CausalScaffold.Flat.TitsNull).

Finite index by compactness: a bounded 'almost-homomorphism into a proper normed ring' gives finite index of the subgroup generated by the eps-near-1 elements (relIndex_closure_ne_zero, pigeonhole through Metric.totallyBounded_iff and QuotientGroup.out_eq').
